newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waigel satisfied with stability pact deal.
newsitem.headline: Waigel satisfied with stability pact deal.

text.p: German finance minister Theo Waigel said he was satisfied with the deal hammered out at on EU summit on a pact to enforce fiscal discipline under monetary union.

"I am satisfied," Waigel told reporters. "It was hard work but successful. It's an important step for the preparation of economic and monetary union (EMU) and it's an important signal for the people and for the markets."

Germany had held out for a tough definition of the precise conditions under which countries should be exempt from fines for running high fiscal deficits after EMU, due to be launched on January 1, 1999.
EU finance ministers wrestled over the issue for 11 hours until early on Friday morning without reaching a final deal.
The ministers and EU leaders took another six hours on Friday to agree that a country would be exempt from fines if gross domestic product (GDP) had fallen by an annual 2.0 percent or more.
If GDP had fallen by between 0.75 and 2.0 percent, ministers would decide whether the country should be fined.
